_about: Sir John Edwin Sandys (1844-1922), Public Orator at Cambridge. Classical scholarship (lane B pivot of 2026-10-10 from translations to public-domain English scholarship on the classics): A History of Classical Scholarship (Cambridge, 3 vols., 1903-1908) and A Short History of Classical Scholarship (1915), raw IA OCR. No uids minted. Round du (2026-10-23), raw IA: Demosthenes against Leptines (1890), Select Private Orations part II (with Paley, 1886; part I is on the f-a-paley shelf), Aristotle's Constitution of Athens (1893), An Easter Vacation in Greece (1887), Harvard Lectures on the Revival of Learning (1905). Not taken: his Bacchae (the open scans OCR its English as Greek letters) and Isocrates Ad Demonicum (same). Round dy (2026-10-23), raw IA: Latin Epigraphy (1919), his school-and-college Orator of Cicero (1885, Latin text with English essays and notes; kept under lane B's extension of Adam's Greek ruling to Latin-dense commentaries), the First Philippic and Olynthiacs (1898 reprint of 1897), his 1909 new edition of Jebb's Theophrastus (the 1870 first edition is on the jebb shelf) and his British Academy lecture on Roger Bacon (1914). Refused: Isocrates Ad Demonicum et Panegyricus (1872; the one scan OCRs its English as Greek letters) and Orationes et Epistolae Cantabrigienses (Latin only).
